name: St. Mary Basilica, Natchez
architect: Robert Cary Long Jr. (design); James Hardie (supervising)
history: The Diocese of Natchez was created in 1837, and work on its cathedral began in 1842. It was dedicated to Our Lady of Sorrows on Christmas Day 1843, but not finished until 1882 and consecrated in 1886. It was the cathedral until 1977 and became a basilica in 1998.
arch: Brick Gothic Revival designed by Robert Cary Long Jr. of Baltimore, with a central square tower and spire set into the front, topped with pinnacles, over a recessed pointed-arch entrance.
features: Bishop John Chanche, Mississippi's first Catholic bishop, was brought back from Baltimore and reburied in the churchyard.
It was restored after damage from a tornado.

look.d: The tower is built into the front wall, crowned with pinnacles.
Begun in 1842, the building was only completed in 1882.

fun: It took forty years to finish.
journal: A Gothic spire over the Mississippi bluffs. Forty years from first brick to last.
